steps.label: Gas pattern
steps.detail: Assess the stomach, proximal bowel and distal gas, including gas in the rectum.
steps.look: Supine (and horizontal-beam) abdominal radiograph: is there dilatation, how many loops, and is there gas in the rectum?
steps.normal: Normal neonatal bowel gas pattern with gas in the rectum.
findings: Double bubble with no distal gas (duodenal atresia pattern).
Few dilated proximal loops (high obstruction).
Many dilated loops with no rectal gas (low obstruction).
steps.tip: The number of dilated loops separates high from low obstruction; the rectal gas tells you whether obstruction is complete.

steps.label: Level of obstruction and cause
steps.detail: Describe the distribution and the likely level, and the transition when demonstrated.
steps.look: Upper GI study for the duodenojejunal flexure position; contrast enema for colon calibre and transition.
steps.normal: No bowel obstruction.
findings: Duodenojejunal flexure right of the left pedicle and below the pylorus: malrotation; corkscrew duodenum suggests midgut volvulus.
Microcolon with filling defects in the terminal ileum (meconium ileus pattern).
Transition zone in the rectosigmoid with a rectosigmoid ratio below 1 (Hirschsprung pattern).
Thickened pyloric muscle __ mm, length __ mm (hypertrophic pyloric stenosis).
steps.tip: Suspected malrotation with volvulus is an emergency; an upper GI study or ultrasound should not wait.

steps.label: Bowel wall
steps.detail: Assess mural abnormalities: pneumatosis, thickening, peristalsis and perfusion when assessed.
steps.look: Radiograph for bubbly or linear intramural gas; ultrasound for wall thickness and Doppler.
steps.normal: No pneumatosis; normal bowel wall on ultrasound where assessed.
findings: Pneumatosis intestinalis in the [right lower quadrant].
Thickened hypoperfused bowel wall on ultrasound.

steps.label: Free gas and fluid
steps.detail: Look for free gas, ascites and collections.
steps.look: Horizontal-beam or left lateral decubitus view; football sign and Rigler sign on supine views.
steps.normal: No free gas or ascites.
findings: Pneumoperitoneum (football sign / Rigler sign).
Complex ascites on ultrasound.

steps.label: Targeted studies and other organs
steps.detail: Record the result of any targeted study, other organ findings and limitations.
steps.look: Ultrasound of the mesenteric vessels (SMV to the right of the SMA; whirlpool sign) when malrotation is suspected.
steps.normal: No targeted study performed.
findings: Whirlpool sign of the mesenteric vessels on ultrasound (midgut volvulus).
SMV lies to the left of the SMA (malrotation).
Incarcerated inguinal hernia.
steps.tip: The gas pattern changes with time and feeding; a normal early radiograph does not exclude an evolving emergency.

model.reporting_aim: Relate the cystic mass to the solid organs, bowel and pelvis to find its organ of origin.

steps.label: Organ of origin
steps.detail: Use continuity and organ displacement to localise the cystic mass.
steps.look: Ultrasound first: claw sign with an organ, bowel continuity, relation to the kidney, ovary and bladder.
findings: Cystic mass arising from the [right] ovary.
Cyst adjacent to the bowel with a gut signature wall (duplication cyst).
Renal cystic mass / hydronephrosis of the [left] kidney.
steps.tip: In children the organ of origin, together with age, narrows the differential more than the cyst appearance.

steps.label: Size and number
steps.detail: Record dimensions, multiplicity and distribution.
steps.look: Three orthogonal dimensions on ultrasound or MRI.
findings: Solitary cyst __ × __ × __ mm.
Multiple non-communicating cysts of varying size (multicystic dysplastic kidney pattern).

steps.label: Wall and contents
steps.detail: Assess simple fluid, septa, debris, fat and solid elements.
steps.look: Ultrasound for echoes and septa; MRI or CT for fat and calcification.
findings: Simple cyst.
Multiseptated cystic mass (lymphatic malformation pattern).
Cyst with fat and calcification (teratoma).
Echogenic layered contents (haemorrhage or debris).

steps.label: Flow and communication
steps.detail: Assess vascularity and any ductal, enteric or collecting-system connection.
steps.look: Doppler of septa and walls; continuity with the bile duct, bowel or renal pelvis.
findings: Cystic dilatation communicating with the common bile duct (choledochal cyst).
Communication with the collecting system (hydronephrosis).
Avascular septa.

steps.label: Mass effect and complications
steps.detail: Assess obstruction, torsion, haemorrhage and inflammation.
steps.look: Adjacent bowel, ureters and vessels; ovarian flow when an adnexal cyst is present.
steps.normal: No mass effect or complication.
findings: Enlarged ovary with peripheral follicles and absent flow (torsion).
Bowel obstruction from the cyst.
Haemorrhage within the cyst.

model.reporting_aim: Relate the mass to the kidneys, adrenals, liver and great vessels to establish its organ of origin.

steps.label: Organ of origin
steps.detail: Identify the dominant organ or retroperitoneal compartment.
steps.look: Ultrasound then MRI: claw sign with the kidney, relation to the adrenal, liver or bowel.
findings: Mass arising from the [right] kidney with a claw sign (nephroblastoma pattern).
Adrenal mass displacing the kidney inferiorly (neuroblastoma pattern).
Mass arising from the liver (hepatoblastoma to be considered in a young child).
steps.tip: Neuroblastoma encases and lifts vessels and crosses the midline; Wilms tumour displaces vessels and arises from the kidney.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Describe size, solid tissue, necrosis, fat, calcification and enhancement.
steps.look: Ultrasound and MRI; CT or radiograph for calcification.
findings: Heterogeneous mass __ × __ × __ mm with calcification (neuroblastoma pattern).
Heterogeneous mass with necrosis and no calcification (Wilms pattern).
Fat and calcification (teratoma).

steps.label: Vessels
steps.detail: Assess displacement, encasement and intravascular extension.
steps.look: Aorta, IVC, coeliac axis, SMA and renal vessels.
steps.normal: No vessel encasement or thrombus.
findings: Encasement of the coeliac axis and SMA.
Tumour thrombus in the IVC.
Displacement of vessels without encasement.

steps.label: Local extent
steps.detail: Assess adjacent organs and neural foramina or spinal canal extension.
steps.look: Axial and coronal MRI through the neural foramina.
steps.normal: No foraminal or spinal extension.
findings: Extension through the neural foramina into the spinal canal (dumbbell).
Invasion of the [liver / kidney].
steps.tip: Intraspinal extension can compress the cord and needs prompt communication.

steps.label: Nodes and spread
steps.detail: Review nodes and covered metastatic sites.
steps.look: Retroperitoneal and mesenteric nodes, liver, bone marrow and lungs when covered.
steps.normal: No nodes or metastases in the field.
findings: Retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.
Liver metastases.
Marrow infiltration.

model.reporting_aim: Relate the tumour to the renal parenchyma, renal vein and IVC, and check the other kidney.

steps.label: Renal origin
steps.detail: Confirm renal origin, side and pole with the claw sign, and measure the mass.
steps.look: Ultrasound and MRI coronal images.
findings: Mass arising from the [left] kidney, [upper] pole, with a claw of renal parenchyma, __ × __ × __ mm.
steps.tip: A claw of renal parenchyma around the mass confirms renal origin.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Describe solid, cystic or necrotic components, enhancement and calcification.
steps.look: MRI T2, DWI and post-contrast images.
findings: Large heterogeneous solid mass with necrosis and haemorrhage (Wilms pattern).
Multilocular cystic mass with thin septa (multilocular cystic renal tumour).
Solid mass in a neonate (mesoblastic nephroma).

steps.label: Other kidney and nephrogenic rests
steps.detail: Assess the remaining renal tissue and the contralateral kidney for further lesions or rests.
steps.look: Both kidneys on T2 and post-contrast images.
steps.normal: Contralateral kidney normal; no further lesions.
findings: Contralateral lesion __ mm (bilateral disease).
Subcapsular homogeneous rests (nephroblastomatosis).
steps.tip: Bilateral disease changes surgical planning; examine the other kidney carefully.

steps.label: Local and venous extent
steps.detail: Assess the capsule, sinus, adjacent tissues and renal vein and IVC thrombus.
steps.look: Renal vein and IVC on ultrasound Doppler and MRI; record the cranial extent of thrombus.
steps.normal: No capsular breach; renal vein and IVC patent.
findings: Tumour thrombus in the renal vein extending into the IVC to the [ ] level.
Tumour rupture with retroperitoneal fluid.

steps.label: Nodes and metastases
steps.detail: Review regional nodes, liver and chest coverage.
steps.look: Retroperitoneal nodes; liver; chest CT for lung metastases.
steps.normal: No nodes or metastases in the covered field.
findings: Enlarged para-aortic nodes.
Lung metastases on chest CT.
Liver metastases.

steps.label: Testes
steps.detail: Record size, echotexture, lie and focal lesions of both testes.
steps.look: Transverse view of both testes side by side for comparison; longitudinal views.
steps.normal: Testes symmetric in size and echotexture with normal lie.
findings: Enlarged heterogeneous [left] testis with a horizontal lie.
Testicular rupture: disrupted tunica albuginea with heterogeneous parenchyma.

steps.label: Perfusion
steps.detail: Compare intratesticular arterial and venous flow with the other side using low-flow settings.
steps.look: Colour or power Doppler with low pulse repetition frequency; spectral waveforms in both testes.
steps.normal: Symmetric intratesticular arterial and venous flow.
findings: Absent intratesticular flow in the [left] testis: testicular torsion.
Reduced flow compared with the other side (partial torsion possible).
Increased flow in the testis and epididymis (orchiepididymitis).
steps.tip: Preserved flow does not exclude partial or intermittent torsion; peripheral hyperaemia is not central perfusion.

steps.label: Spermatic cord and epididymis
steps.detail: Look for twisting of the cord, epididymal enlargement or hyperaemia, and hernia.
steps.look: Follow the cord from the inguinal canal to the testis for a whirlpool sign.
steps.normal: Straight spermatic cord; epididymis normal; no hernia.
findings: Whirlpool sign of the spermatic cord (torsion).
Enlarged hyperaemic epididymis (epididymitis).
Inguinoscrotal hernia containing [bowel / omentum].
steps.tip: The whirlpool sign of the cord is the most specific sign of torsion.

steps.label: Focal lesion
steps.detail: Describe any focal lesion as intratesticular or extratesticular with size and vascularity.
steps.look: Grayscale and Doppler of any focal lesion.
steps.normal: No focal lesion.
findings: Avascular nodule at the upper pole with surrounding hyperaemia (torsed appendix testis).
Intratesticular solid vascular mass __ mm.
Intratesticular haematoma.

steps.label: Extratesticular findings
steps.detail: Evaluate hydrocele, haematocele, scrotal wall, collections and varicocele.
steps.look: Scrotal wall thickness; fluid around the testis; veins with Valsalva.
steps.normal: No hydrocele or scrotal wall thickening.
findings: Reactive hydrocele.
Haematocele.
Scrotal wall oedema without testicular abnormality (idiopathic scrotal oedema).

steps.label: Technique and lung volume
steps.detail: Assess rotation, inspiration and lung expansion.
steps.look: Anterior rib ends and clavicles for rotation; count ribs above the diaphragm.
steps.normal: Supine AP radiograph without rotation; normal lung volumes.
findings: Low lung volumes.
Hyperinflated lungs.
Rotated to the [right].
steps.tip: Rotation and low volumes mimic disease in neonates.

steps.label: Lung pattern
steps.detail: Describe diffuse or focal opacity, air bronchograms and lucencies.
steps.look: Compare both lungs; look for granularity, streaky interstitial opacities or patchy asymmetric opacity.
steps.normal: Lungs clear.
findings: Diffuse granular (ground-glass) opacity with air bronchograms and low volumes (respiratory distress syndrome pattern).
Streaky perihilar opacity with fluid in the fissures and normal or increased volume (transient tachypnoea pattern).
Patchy asymmetric opacity with hyperinflation (meconium aspiration pattern).
Coarse reticular opacity with cystic lucencies (bronchopulmonary dysplasia).

steps.label: Air leak and pleura
steps.detail: Assess pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, interstitial emphysema and effusion.
steps.look: Anterior pneumothorax on the supine film: a hyperlucent hemithorax and sharp heart border.
steps.normal: No pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum or effusion.
findings: [Right] pneumothorax.
Pneumomediastinum lifting the thymus (spinnaker-sail sign).
Pulmonary interstitial emphysema of the [ ] lung.
steps.tip: On a supine neonatal film, a pneumothorax collects anteriorly: look for a sharp heart border and hyperlucency.

steps.label: Heart, thymus and diaphragm
steps.detail: Assess the cardiothymic silhouette and diaphragm position.
steps.look: Cardiothymic contour; bowel loops in the chest.
steps.normal: Normal cardiothymic silhouette and diaphragm.
findings: Bowel loops in the left hemithorax with mediastinal shift (congenital diaphragmatic hernia).
Cardiomegaly with increased pulmonary vascularity.

steps.label: Lines and tubes
steps.detail: Trace each device and locate its tip using the film anatomy.
steps.look: Endotracheal tube between the thoracic inlet and carina; UVC tip at the IVC–right atrial junction; UAC in the high (thoracic) or low (below renal arteries) position; gastric tube in the stomach.
steps.normal: No lines or tubes. / All lines and tubes in satisfactory position.
findings: Endotracheal tube tip at [T2], above the carina.
Umbilical venous catheter tip projects over the [liver / portal vein]; not in the IVC.
Umbilical arterial catheter tip at [T8] (high position).
Gastric tube coiled in an upper oesophageal pouch (oesophageal atresia).
steps.tip: An umbilical arterial catheter goes down into the pelvis first (via the iliac artery); a venous catheter goes straight up through the liver.

steps.label: Bowel gas pattern
steps.detail: Assess distension and persistent focal loops on serial films.
steps.look: Serial supine radiographs; a fixed dilated loop unchanged for 24 hours is concerning.
steps.normal: Normal bowel gas pattern.
findings: Diffuse bowel distension.
Persistent fixed dilated loop in the [right lower quadrant].
Gasless abdomen.

steps.label: Pneumatosis and wall
steps.detail: Look for intramural gas and wall abnormalities.
steps.look: Bubbly or linear lucency in the bowel wall on radiographs; ultrasound for wall thickness and echogenic dots.
steps.normal: No pneumatosis.
findings: Pneumatosis intestinalis in the [right lower quadrant / diffuse].
Thickened / thinned bowel wall on ultrasound.
steps.tip: Bubbly pneumatosis can look like stool; compare with the clinical picture and serial films.

steps.label: Portal venous gas
steps.detail: Assess branching gas in the liver on radiograph or echogenic moving foci on ultrasound.
steps.look: Right upper quadrant on radiograph; portal vein on ultrasound.
steps.normal: No portal venous gas.
findings: Branching lucencies over the liver (portal venous gas).
Echogenic foci moving in the portal vein on ultrasound.

steps.label: Free air and fluid
steps.detail: Look for pneumoperitoneum, ascites and collections.
steps.look: Horizontal-beam or left-side-down decubitus view; ultrasound for complex fluid.
steps.normal: No free air or complex fluid.
findings: Pneumoperitoneum (football / Rigler sign): perforation.
Complex ascites with debris.
Localised collection.
steps.tip: Perforation is a surgical emergency; a horizontal-beam view is the most sensitive radiograph.

steps.label: Ultrasound and evolution
steps.detail: When obtained, assess perfusion and peristalsis, and describe change over time.
steps.look: Doppler of bowel wall; comparison with previous films.
steps.normal: Ultrasound not performed. No interval change.
findings: Absent bowel wall perfusion in the [ ] (necrosis).
Worsening since [time].
Improving pattern.

steps.label: Compartment and thymus
steps.detail: Localise the mass and distinguish it from normal thymus.
steps.look: Anterior mediastinum: normal thymus is soft, conforms to adjacent structures and does not compress the airway or vessels.
steps.normal: Normal thymus for age; no mediastinal mass.
findings: Anterior mediastinal mass separate from normal thymus.
Middle mediastinal cyst adjacent to the carina.
Posterior mediastinal paravertebral mass.
steps.tip: Normal thymus never compresses the airway or vessels; a mass that does is not normal thymus.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Assess soft tissue, fluid, fat and calcification.
steps.look: CT attenuation or MRI signal.
findings: Homogeneous soft-tissue mass __ mm (lymphoma pattern).
Fat, fluid and calcification (germ cell tumour / teratoma).
Fluid-filled cyst (bronchogenic / foregut duplication cyst).
Calcified paravertebral mass (neuroblastoma pattern).

steps.label: Airway
steps.detail: Describe tracheobronchial displacement or narrowing.
steps.look: Axial and coronal CT at the narrowest airway; minimum intensity projections.
steps.normal: No airway narrowing.
findings: Tracheal narrowing to __ mm (cross-sectional area reduced by about __%).
Compression of the [left main] bronchus with distal air trapping.
steps.tip: Significant airway compression by an anterior mass is a major anaesthetic risk; communicate it directly.

steps.label: Vessels and spinal canal
steps.detail: Assess vessel compression and paravertebral or foraminal extension.
steps.look: Superior vena cava and pulmonary arteries; neural foramina on MRI.
steps.normal: No vascular compression; no intraspinal extension.
findings: Compression of the superior vena cava.
Extension through the neural foramina into the spinal canal.

steps.label: Nodes and spread
steps.detail: Review nodes, pleura, pericardium and other lesions.
steps.look: Hilar and mediastinal nodes; pleural and pericardial effusions.
steps.normal: No lymphadenopathy, effusion or other lesion.
findings: Bulky mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy.
Pleural / pericardial effusion.

steps.label: Airways
steps.detail: Assess airway anatomy, narrowing and abnormal bronchial branching.
steps.look: Minimum intensity projections and multiplanar reformats.
steps.normal: Normal airway anatomy and calibre.
findings: Tracheal bronchus to the right upper lobe.
Bronchial atresia with a mucocele and surrounding hyperlucency.
Tracheal narrowing to __ mm.

steps.label: Lung parenchyma
steps.detail: Describe focal or diffuse patterns, nodules and cysts with their distribution.
steps.look: Thin-section lung windows.
steps.normal: Lungs clear.
findings: Multicystic lesion in the [left lower lobe] (congenital pulmonary airway malformation pattern).
Hyperlucent overinflated [left upper] lobe (congenital lobar overinflation).
Consolidation / nodules in the [ ].

steps.label: Vessels and congenital anomalies
steps.detail: Describe relevant vessels and congenital abnormalities within technique limits.
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced images for systemic arterial supply and venous drainage.
steps.normal: No vascular anomaly.
findings: Systemic arterial supply from the descending aorta to a [left lower lobe] lesion (sequestration).
Vascular ring / sling compressing the airway.
steps.tip: Look for a systemic feeding artery from the aorta: it defines a sequestration and matters for surgery.

steps.label: Mediastinum and pleura
steps.detail: Review the age-appropriate thymus, nodes and pleural space.
steps.look: Mediastinal windows.
steps.normal: Normal thymus for age; no lymphadenopathy or pleural abnormality.
findings: Mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
Empyema with split pleura sign.
Pleural effusion.

steps.label: Chest wall and comparison
steps.detail: Inspect the chest wall, bones and interval change, and note limitations.
steps.look: Bone windows; prior studies.
steps.normal: Chest wall and bones normal. No significant motion or atelectasis limitation.
findings: Dependent atelectasis (sedation) limits assessment of the posterior lungs.
Pectus excavatum.
Interval change since [date].
steps.tip: Sedation-related dependent atelectasis can mimic disease; prone images or comparison help.

steps.label: Survey completeness
steps.detail: Check that every required skeletal survey view was obtained, and record repeats and omissions.
steps.look: Follow the local safeguarding skeletal survey protocol view by view: skull, chest and ribs (including obliques), spine, pelvis and each limb segment.
steps.normal: Complete skeletal survey according to [protocol]; all views diagnostic.
findings: Views [ ] repeated because of positioning.
Views [ ] not obtained: [reason].
steps.tip: An incomplete survey must be declared; omissions can matter in court.

steps.label: Fracture inventory
steps.detail: Describe each injury objectively by side, bone, segment, morphology and displacement.
steps.look: Metaphyses of long bones for classic metaphyseal lesions; posterior and lateral ribs; skull.
steps.normal: No fracture identified.
findings: Classic metaphyseal lesion (corner / bucket-handle) of the [right distal femur].
Posterior rib fractures of the [left 6th–8th] ribs.
Complex skull fracture of the [ ] bone.
Transverse fracture of the [ ] diaphysis.
steps.tip: Classic metaphyseal lesions and posterior rib fractures have high specificity for inflicted injury in infants.

steps.label: Healing features
steps.detail: Describe periosteal reaction, callus and remodelling without assigning an exact date.
steps.look: Each fracture for periosteal new bone and callus; comparison with earlier imaging.
steps.normal: No healing features.
findings: Periosteal new bone along the [ ] without callus.
Fractures at different stages of healing.
Healing fracture not visible on the study of [date].
steps.tip: Imaging can describe healing features but cannot give an exact date of injury.

steps.label: Bone quality and mimics
steps.detail: Assess mineralisation, dysplasia, metabolic bone disease and normal developmental variants.
steps.look: Bone density, skull (wormian bones), metaphyseal shape and physiological periosteal reaction in young infants.
steps.normal: Normal mineralisation; no dysplasia or metabolic bone disease.
findings: Osteopenia with wormian bones (osteogenesis imperfecta to be considered).
Metaphyseal changes of rickets.
Symmetric physiological periosteal new bone (normal variant in young infants).

steps.label: Associated studies
steps.detail: Review the neuroimaging, spine and visceral imaging actually obtained.
steps.look: Brain CT or MRI; spine imaging; abdominal imaging when performed.
steps.normal: No neuroimaging, spinal or visceral imaging obtained.
findings: Subdural haematomas of different signal / density on brain imaging.
Abdominal visceral injury on CT.

steps.label: Safeguarding handover
steps.detail: Record the objective imaging concern and its direct communication, and further imaging required by the pathway.
steps.look: Local safeguarding pathway; follow-up skeletal survey after about two weeks where required.
steps.normal: No imaging features of concern.
findings: Findings communicated to [named recipient, team] on [date and time].
Follow-up skeletal survey recommended in about [two weeks] according to local protocol.
steps.tip: Imaging cannot determine intent or perpetrator; describe findings objectively.

steps.label: Suture inventory
steps.detail: Assess the metopic, sagittal, both coronal and both lambdoid sutures individually.
steps.look: Axial CT source images and 3D rendering; ultrasound for sutures in young infants.
steps.normal: All cranial sutures patent.
findings: Fused sagittal suture; other sutures patent.
Fused [right] coronal suture.
Fused metopic suture with a ridge.
steps.tip: The metopic suture normally closes in infancy; a closed metopic suture alone is not trigonocephaly.

steps.label: Extent of fusion
steps.detail: Describe the affected segment, length of fusion, ridge or sclerosis and confirm on source images.
steps.look: Source images along each suture; 3D rendering can hide thin patent sutures.
findings: Complete fusion of the sagittal suture with ridging.
Partial fusion of the [posterior] third of the sagittal suture.
steps.tip: 3D segmentation can erase a thin patent suture or create an apparent gap; confirm on source images.

steps.label: Vault shape
steps.detail: Describe the skull shape pattern, asymmetry and compensatory growth.
steps.look: Vertex view of the 3D rendering; cephalic index with named landmarks if used.
steps.normal: Normal skull shape.
findings: Scaphocephaly (long narrow skull) from sagittal synostosis.
Trigonocephaly with a triangular forehead from metopic synostosis.
Anterior plagiocephaly from unilateral coronal synostosis.
Parallelogram shape without suture fusion (positional plagiocephaly).
steps.tip: Positional plagiocephaly gives a parallelogram shape with the ear moved forward; lambdoid synostosis gives a trapezoid with the ear moved back.

steps.label: Orbits and skull base
steps.detail: Assess orbital asymmetry, cranial fossae and skull-base findings.
steps.look: Frontal and basal views; orbital shape (harlequin eye in coronal synostosis).
steps.normal: Symmetric orbits and skull base.
findings: Harlequin-eye deformity of the [right] orbit.
Hypotelorism (metopic synostosis).

steps.label: Intracranial and associated findings
steps.detail: Describe ventricles and other visible abnormality, and whether the pattern is single-suture or multisuture.
steps.look: Brain window of the CT or MRI.
steps.normal: No intracranial abnormality within the limits of the study; single-suture pattern.
findings: Multisuture synostosis, raising concern for a syndromic form.
Copper-beaten appearance of the inner table (raised intracranial pressure to be considered).
Chiari I malformation.

steps.label: Standard plane
steps.detail: Confirm a valid standard coronal plane before measuring.
steps.look: Straight horizontal iliac line, lower limb of the ilium, and the acetabular labrum all visible (Graf standard plane).
steps.normal: Standard plane obtained on both sides.
findings: Standard plane not obtained on the [ ] side; measurements are not reliable.
steps.tip: Measurements from an invalid plane misclassify the hip; do not categorise without the standard plane.

steps.label: Bony roof (alpha angle)
steps.detail: Assess acetabular morphology and measure the alpha angle.
steps.look: Alpha angle between the baseline (iliac line) and the bony roof line.
steps.normal: Right alpha angle __°, left __°; good bony roof.
findings: Alpha angle __° (50–59°): physiologically immature under 3 months (Graf IIa) or delayed ossification over 3 months (IIb).
Alpha angle __° (43–49°): critical hip (Graf IIc) or decentring (D).
Alpha angle below 43°: decentred hip (Graf III / IV).
steps.tip: An alpha angle of 60° or more is normal (Graf I).

steps.label: Cartilaginous roof
steps.detail: Assess the labrum and cartilaginous coverage (beta angle if used).
steps.look: Cartilage roof line from the bony rim to the labrum.
steps.normal: Cartilaginous roof covers the femoral head; labrum in normal position.
findings: Beta angle __°.
Labrum everted (Graf III) / inverted (Graf IV).

steps.label: Femoral head position
steps.detail: Describe centring and femoral head coverage.
steps.look: Proportion of the femoral head medial to the iliac line.
steps.normal: Femoral heads centred with coverage of 50% or more.
findings: [Left] femoral head coverage __%, decentred.

steps.label: Stability and classification
steps.detail: Record stability only if examined, and interpret morphology with age.
steps.look: Stress manoeuvre in the transverse flexion view when performed.
steps.normal: Stable hips on dynamic assessment. Graf type I bilaterally at age [ ] weeks.
findings: [Left] hip subluxable on stress.
Dynamic assessment not performed.
Graf type [ ] at age [ ] weeks.

steps.label: Alignment and development
steps.detail: Assess joint alignment and age-appropriate ossification, comparing both hips.
steps.look: AP pelvis and frog-leg lateral; Klein line along the superior femoral neck.
steps.normal: Normal alignment and ossification; symmetric hips.
findings: Klein line does not intersect the [left] femoral epiphysis (slipped capital femoral epiphysis).
Asymmetric ossification of the femoral heads.
steps.tip: The frog-leg lateral is more sensitive for early slipped capital femoral epiphysis than the AP view.

steps.label: Epiphysis and physis
steps.detail: Assess femoral head contour, physis width and displacement.
steps.look: Epiphyseal height and density; physis width compared with the other side.
steps.normal: Normal femoral epiphyses and physes.
findings: Flattening, sclerosis and fragmentation of the [right] femoral epiphysis (Perthes disease).
Widened irregular physis with posteromedial slip of the epiphysis.

steps.label: Effusion
steps.detail: Describe effusion and synovial findings, comparing both sides.
steps.look: Anterior sagittal ultrasound along the femoral neck; compare capsule distance with the other hip.
steps.normal: No hip effusion.
findings: [Right] hip effusion (capsule-to-neck distance __ mm; __ mm more than the other side).
Synovial thickening with hyperaemia.
steps.tip: An effusion alone cannot separate transient synovitis from septic arthritis; aspiration is guided by the clinical picture.

steps.label: Bone and marrow
steps.detail: Review osseous change and MRI marrow findings if obtained.
steps.look: Radiographs for lucency and periosteal reaction; MRI for marrow oedema and epiphyseal perfusion.
steps.normal: No bone or marrow abnormality.
findings: Metaphyseal marrow oedema with periosteal reaction (osteomyelitis).
Reduced epiphyseal enhancement (ischaemia).
Avulsion of the [anterior inferior iliac spine / ischial apophysis].

steps.label: Soft tissues and comparison
steps.detail: Inspect adjacent muscles and collections and note change over time.
steps.look: Periarticular muscles and fascial planes on ultrasound or MRI.
steps.normal: No soft-tissue collection; no change since [date].
findings: Intramuscular abscess in the [obturator internus].
Interval progression since [date].

steps.label: Ventricles
steps.detail: Measure ventricular size with a named method and compare with an age chart and prior scans.
steps.look: Coronal view at the level of the foramen of Monro for the ventricular index; sagittal views for the anterior horns.
steps.normal: Ventricles normal in size and symmetric.
findings: Ventricular index __ mm (above the 97th centile for gestational age).
Progressive ventricular dilatation since [date].
steps.tip: Serial measurements with the same method and chart matter more than a single value.

steps.label: Germinal matrix and intraventricular haemorrhage
steps.detail: Inspect the caudothalamic grooves and ventricular contents.
steps.look: Coronal and parasagittal views of the caudothalamic groove.
steps.normal: No germinal matrix or intraventricular haemorrhage.
findings: Germinal matrix haemorrhage at the [right] caudothalamic groove (grade I).
Intraventricular haemorrhage filling less than half of the ventricle (grade II).
Intraventricular haemorrhage with ventricular dilatation (grade III).

steps.label: Parenchymal injury
steps.detail: Assess periventricular echogenicity, cysts and focal haemorrhagic infarction.
steps.look: Parasagittal views of the periventricular white matter compared with the choroid plexus.
steps.normal: Normal periventricular white matter.
findings: Periventricular echogenicity (flaring) — follow up to assess evolution.
Periventricular cysts (cystic periventricular leukomalacia).
Periventricular haemorrhagic infarction on the [ ] side.
steps.tip: Periventricular flaring is only significant if it persists or evolves into cysts on follow-up.

steps.label: Midline and deep structures
steps.detail: Review midline anatomy and the deep grey matter.
steps.look: Midsagittal view: corpus callosum, cavum septi pellucidi, cerebellar vermis; coronal views of the basal ganglia.
steps.normal: Normal midline structures and deep grey matter.
findings: Cavum septi pellucidi and cavum vergae (normal variant).
Linear echogenic lenticulostriate vessels (mineralising vasculopathy).
Absent corpus callosum.

steps.label: Posterior fossa, extra-axial spaces and limitations
steps.detail: Assess the posterior fossa via the mastoid window, extra-axial spaces and coverage limits.
steps.look: Mastoid fontanelle for the cerebellum and fourth ventricle; high-frequency probe for extra-axial spaces.
steps.normal: Normal posterior fossa and extra-axial spaces.
findings: Cerebellar haemorrhage.
Widened subarachnoid spaces (benign enlargement in macrocrania).
Posterior fossa not assessed.

steps.label: Levels and window
steps.detail: Establish vertebral levels with reproducible landmarks and describe the acoustic window.
steps.look: Count from the last rib-bearing vertebra or up from the coccyx and sacrum; mark the skin.
steps.normal: Levels counted from [ ]; good acoustic window.
findings: Transitional anatomy; counting uncertain.
Limited window above [ ].

steps.label: Conus medullaris
steps.detail: Describe the conus level, shape, position and motion.
steps.look: Longitudinal midline images; real-time pulsation of the cord and roots.
steps.normal: Conus terminates at [L1–L2] with normal tapering shape and normal pulsation.
findings: Conus terminates low at [L3], with reduced motion (tethering to be considered).
Blunted conus terminus.
steps.tip: A conus at or above the L2–L3 level is normal in a newborn; a low, fixed conus suggests tethering.

steps.label: Filum and cauda equina
steps.detail: Assess filum thickness, echogenicity and root mobility.
steps.look: True transverse image of the filum; real-time root motion.
steps.normal: Filum under 2 mm, normal echogenicity; mobile nerve roots.
findings: Thickened (__ mm) echogenic filum (fibrolipoma / fatty filum).
Nerve roots clumped and immobile.

steps.label: Cutaneous tract and posterior elements
steps.detail: Trace any tract from the skin marker and assess posterior element defects.
steps.look: Longitudinal and transverse images at the skin marker.
steps.normal: No sinus tract; posterior elements intact.
findings: Dorsal dermal sinus tract from the skin to the [spinal canal / dura].
Posterior element defect at [ ].
Simple coccygeal pit ending blindly below the canal.
steps.tip: A tract entering the spinal canal is a risk for infection and needs prompt referral.

steps.label: Associated anomalies and limitations
steps.detail: Review lipoma, split cord, syrinx and limitations requiring MRI.
steps.look: Transverse images of the cord; the lumbosacral canal.
steps.normal: No lipoma, split cord or syrinx.
findings: Intraspinal lipoma __ × __ × __ mm.
Split cord (diastematomyelia).
Dilated central canal / syrinx.
MRI recommended because of [limitation / finding].

model.reporting_aim: Locate the organ being measured and compare it with an age- or height-matched reference.

steps.label: Age and clinical question
steps.detail: Record chronological (and corrected) age, body size where relevant and the clinical question.
steps.look: Referral information; height or weight when the reference requires it.
findings: Age [ ] (corrected [ ]); height [ ] cm; question: [ ].

steps.label: Age-appropriate anatomy
steps.detail: Distinguish normal development and variants from pathology.
steps.look: Appearance expected for age (for example prominent renal pyramids and thymus in infants).
steps.normal: Appearances appropriate for age.
findings: Hypoechoic prominent renal pyramids (normal in infants).
Normal thymus extending into the [ ].
steps.tip: Normal infant anatomy — hypoechoic pyramids, a large thymus — can mimic disease.

steps.label: Target organ findings
steps.detail: Describe the organ in question and any focal or diffuse abnormality.
steps.look: Use the organ-specific module for a full report.
steps.normal: Target organ normal.
findings: [Organ]: [ ].

steps.label: Measurements and reference
steps.detail: Measure in the same plane as the reference and state the reference used.
steps.look: Named reference chart by age, height or body surface area.
findings: [Kidney] length __ mm, within the range for age [ ] ([reference]).
[Spleen] length __ mm, above the upper limit for age.

steps.label: Associated findings and limits
steps.detail: Record associated findings, limitations and remaining questions.
steps.look: Structures not visualised; motion or window limits.
steps.normal: No associated findings; no significant limitation.
findings: Limited by [motion / bowel gas]; [ ] not visualised.
Associated finding: [ ].
